sources.paper_title: CryptGPU: Fast Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning on the GPU
sources.publication: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy 2021
sources.reported_or_reproduced: reported_by_original_CryptGPU_paper; PEA runtime-to-accuracy statement retained separately as a secondary contextual claim
sources.model: VGG-16 modified for CIFAR-10 with average pooling
sources.privacy_scope: three-party MPC confidentiality against one semi-honest corruption; no differential privacy guarantee
sources.mpc_setting: 2-out-of-3 replicated secret sharing over Z_(2^64), 20 fractional bits
sources.runtime: 12.14 seconds for one private-training iteration at batch size 32
sources.communication: 7.55 GB per private-training iteration at batch size 32
sources.hardware: three AWS p3.2xlarge instances; each has one NVIDIA Tesla V100 16 GB, 8 Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 2.3 GHz CPUs, and 61 GB RAM; LAN 1.25 GB/s and 0.2 ms average latency
sources.source_location: CryptGPU experiments.tex, experimental setup and Table tab:training-comp; accuracy.tex, Table tab:pooling
sources.secondary_PEA_claim: PEA states about 12 seconds per iteration and more than 16 hours for a non-private VGG-16 to reach about 88%; this is not a directly reported CryptGPU accuracy-runtime point and must not be represented as one.
sources.comparability: Textual system background only. Different deep model, GPU hardware, protocol, privacy scope, batch size, communication topology, and timing boundary. Never divide this runtime by local runtime or claim a strict speedup.
